newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks skyrocket to record high close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks skyrocket to record high close.

text.p: Mexican stocks notched up their biggest single-day gain ever in terms of points Wednesday, racing to a record close as optimism about Mexico led to a foreign investor feeding frenzy.
The blue-chip IPC share index climbed 176.74 points, or 3.68 percent, to a record 4,974.23. It was a historic rise in points and the sharpest percentage increase since Jan. 2, 1996.
"They are loving us," a happy floor trader said of foreign buyers. Trading volume was very heavy at 193 million, and winners pounded losers 87 to 23.
Local and foreign investors snapped up stocks to juggle portfolios in the wake of second-quarter earnings reports that showed companies were finally climbing out of Mexico's long recession.
Also helping were a big drop in domestic interest rates, while bank stocks soared on news the country's second largest bank would tackle its past-due mortgage loan problems.
The previous closing record of 4,862.39 points was set July 10, when the market rallied after the Mexican midterm elections. Later, volatility set in amid concerns over plunging Brazilian equities.

"Investors are shifting portfolio allocations on the basis of second-quarter earnings, and naturally the international scene is overwhelmingly favourable," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
"Rock-bottom long bond yields and a record rise on Wall Street made Mexican ADRs (American Depositatry Receipts) very attractively priced for international investors," he said.
The bourse has also been helped by a gale-force tailwind blowing from bullish U.S. markets, analysts said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 80.36 points to 8,254.89, while the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was 25/32 higher in late trading, pushing the yield down to 6.33 percent.
The euphoria did not affect other Latin American markets, however. Mexico was the only standout on Wednesday while Argentina, Brazil and Peru stayed flat.
Rojas said Tuesday night's decline in benchmark domestic interest rates to their lowest level since Mexico's 1994 peso devaluation crisis also kept the bulls charging.
"The fact the peso withstood the drop in Cetes (Mexican treasury bond) rates shows there is room for them to fall further," he said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts softened 0.5 centavos at the close but were still close to their strongest level for the year at 7.7825/7.7900 per dollar.
Dealers said several market heavyweights posted record high closes, including Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), financial group Bancomer and conglomerate Carso.
Telmex climbed 80 centavos (10 cents) to 21.40 pesos ($2.75), while Telmex's ADRs jumped 1-9/16 to 54-5/16.
Bancomer soared 60 centavos (8 cents) to 5.48 pesos (70 cents) as domestic interest rates fell and the bank announced a fresh mortage debt restructuring programme, traders said.

Carso rose 3.10 pesos (40 cents) to 62.00 pesos ($7.96). The gain came after the conglomerate said in a conference call that it expected income soon from deals to sell interests in its subsidiaries, dealers said.
